**Finding submitted: compliant** (confidence 0.86)

The planner's `likelyAbsent` hint was wrong — the flat single-section outline hid a full indemnity regime at Sections 10–11. Verifying against the full text rather than the outline was decisive here.

Why this clears the rule:

| Preferred element | Status |
|---|---|
| Vendor defends/indemnifies Customer + related persons | ✅ p0047 (extends to officers, directors, managers, members, agents, employees) |
| Third-party IP infringement | ✅ Unqualified "Services"/"Auction Platform" prongs + warranty prong (iv) tied to the p0033 non-infringement warranty |
| Vendor breach of law | ✅ Via prong (iv) → p0037/p0041 compliance warranties |
| Data breach caused by Vendor | ✅ Via prong (iv) → p0035 security warranty |
| Gross negligence / wilful misconduct | ✅ Prong (v) acts or omissions |
| Standard procedure | ✅ p0053–p0055 |

Two points worth flagging to the deal team as *better* than our fallback: indemnification is expressly carved out of the consequential-damages waiver (p0027), and there is **no aggregate liability cap anywhere in the agreement** — so Kubient's indemnity is uncapped rather than subject to a 3× super-cap.

The one genuine gap is that AP's indemnity (p0052) is reciprocal rather than narrowed to AP content and breach of law. I made a deliberate judgement not to redline it: the prongs mirror Kubient's own, AP already accepts sole liability for Content and Properties at p0025 and warrants their non-infringement at p0043–p0044, and opening a symmetric clause when the Vendor side is uncapped and broader than our model language invites Kubient to trim its own obligations. That trade-off is documented in the rationale so counsel can override if they want to press it.
